```
#!/bin/bash -l

# Flux directives translated from PBS
# The PBS request for 3 nodes with 128 PPN is translated to 3 nodes and
# a total of 384 tasks. Flux will distribute them evenly (128 tasks/node).
#FLUX: -N 3
#FLUX: -n 384
#FLUX: -t 1:00:00
#FLUX: -q starq

#
# --- Omitted PBS options and explanations ---
#
# -l mem=64gb
#   Omitted. Flux does not have a direct batch script directive for memory.
#   The original job requested 64GB of memory, likely per node.
#   Performance implication: Without a memory constraint, the job may be
#   scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, potentially causing it to
#   fail with an out-of-memory error or perform poorly due to heavy swapping.
#
# -r n
#   Omitted. Job rerunnability is not typically specified via a batch directive
#   in Flux.
#
# -j oe
#   Omitted. Flux combines stdout and stderr into a single output file by default
#   when no error file (-e) is specified.
#

# go to your working directory containing the batch script, code and data
cd /fs/lustre/cita/zack/jl/dev/LagrangianPerturbationTheory/projectamd
module load openmpi

julia --project -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.instantiate()'
julia --project -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.precompile()'

# WARNING: The job allocates 384 tasks (3 nodes * 128 tasks/node) but only
# launches the parallel application on 192 tasks. This will leave 192 task
# slots idle, which is an inefficient use of resources.
# The custom launcher 'mpiexecjl' has been replaced by the standard 'flux run'.
# The '--project' flag is passed to the julia executable.
flux run -n 192 julia --project fft_filter_6144.jl

```
